Detection only. This app observes and blocks known infrastructure; it cannot remove an implant already present. If a full chain is observed, treat the device as compromised and seek expert help.
Android permits one active VPN per device. The DNS scanner and a WireGuard tunnel cannot run at the same time — this screen switches between them explicitly.
DNS monitoring is paused while the tunnel is up. Your traffic is encrypted to the provider, but this app no longer sees your lookups, so AdFection indicators cannot be matched.
No profiles yet. Import a WireGuard .conf from your provider, or paste one in.

Cloudflare WARP (free, generated on this device)

Registers a WARP account directly from the app — the same two API calls wgcf makes — and stores the profile in app-private storage, so no .conf is ever copied around. Requires no account, no email and no payment. Caveat: Cloudflare refuses WireGuard handshakes in some regions as abuse prevention, and newly provisioned accounts are being issued the MASQUE transport, which WireGuard cannot use. Run "Check WARP status" while connected to find out which you are getting.
No WARP account on this device.
— measured before the tunnel dropped; your traffic is now going direct.
The stored account and its credentials are deleted from this app. The WireGuard profile stays on disk until you delete it from the list, and your Cloudflare account itself is unaffected.
Only services that publish WireGuard configuration files are listed, because those are the ones this app can import. Each entry states what the operator can see about you.

Private DNS is bypassing this scanner
Private DNS mode is \'%1$s\' (%2$s). Android sends DNS over TLS straight to that resolver, so queries never reach the scanner\'s DNS interface. Monitoring will look \'broken\' while this is on.
Settings \u2192 Network & internet \u2192 Private DNS \u2192 set to \'Off\' while using this scanner. Then restart protection.
This is the identifier Discover-Tech used to select individual devices for infection. With it enabled, your device can be singled out in ad auctions.
Settings \u2192 Privacy \u2192 Ads \u2192 Delete advertising ID (or opt out of ads personalization).
Advertising ID state could not be read
The OS did not expose \'limit_ad_tracking\'. Some OEM builds rename this key; verify ad personalization manually.
Accessibility service with suggestive name enabled
Enabled services include %1$s. Accessibility services can read everything on screen and tap on your behalf.
Settings \u2192 Accessibility \u2192 review every enabled service and disable anything you did not deliberately install.
This app (or another) can draw over other apps
Overlay permission is a common component of credential-stealing implants.
Settings \u2192 Apps \u2192 Special access \u2192 Display over other apps.
USB debugging permits app installation and data extraction by anyone with physical access and an authorised host key.
Disable USB debugging unless you are actively developing.
Install from unknown sources is allowed
Sideloaded APKs bypass store review and are how most implants arrive.
Another VPN is holding the single VPN slot
\'%1$s\' is the active VPN. Android permits one active VPN per user, so this scanner cannot see any DNS traffic while it is running. Queries to known spyware infrastructure are going unobserved.
Either stop \'%1$s\' and start this scanner, or switch to the tunnel screen and accept that DNS matching is paused. The two modes are mutually exclusive on Android.
No AdFection scanner VPN is running. Without it, queries to known spyware infrastructure go unobserved.
Start the scanner from the main screen.

Settings \u2192 System \u2192 System update \u2192 enable automatic updates.
Android can suspend a background VPN service to save power. While it is suspended the scanner sees no DNS traffic, yet the notification still says protection is active.
Settings \u2192 Apps \u2192 AdFection Scanner \u2192 Battery \u2192 Unrestricted. Then restart protection.
Protection does not survive a reboot
This app is not the always-on VPN, so monitoring stops at restart and stays off until it is started by hand.

Settings \u2192 Network & internet \u2192 VPN \u2192 AdFection Scanner \u2192 enable \'Always-on VPN\'. Note this also prevents any other VPN (including the WireGuard tunnel screen) from taking the slot.
Free on Oracle Cloud Always Free tier; otherwise about $4/month for any small VPS.
Install wg-easy (Docker) or Defguard on a small server, or run wg-quick directly. The panel generates the .conf for each device.
You. Nobody else. No third party is in the path.
The only option with no third party to trust. Best choice if you can spend an hour setting it up — and the right one for journalists, lawyers and activists.
Genuinely free, no paid tier, no account purchase.

Use \'Register WARP account\' on the VPN screen. The app performs the same registration wgcf does, then stores the profile in its own private storage — there is no file to copy and no terminal involved.

Cloudflare terminates your traffic and sees your source IP and destinations. WARP is not a normal VPN: it is Cloudflare\'s network, and their privacy policy governs it. It also does not hide your IP from Cloudflare.

The best genuinely-free option, because the generator is open source and auditable. Do not treat it as anonymity against Cloudflare itself. One caveat: Cloudflare refuses WireGuard handshakes in some regions as abuse prevention, and new accounts are being issued the MASQUE transport, which WireGuard cannot speak — use the status check to see which you get.
Free tier is permanent, no data cap. Paid tiers add servers and features.
Create a free account, then account.protonvpn.com → Downloads → WireGuard configuration → Create. The free plan can generate configs with fewer options.
Proton. They publish audits, are based in Switzerland, and their clients are open source, but they still terminate the tunnel.
A credible free option with real audits behind it — the honest choice when self-hosting is not possible and Cloudflare is not acceptable.
5 EUR per month flat, no free tier.
Create an account number (no email required), then generate WireGuard configs from the account page.
Mullvad, who by design cannot tie an account to a person. Payment and account are decoupled.
Best-in-class for metadata minimisation. If you can pay 5 EUR, this is the strongest off-the-shelf choice.
Create an account, then generate WireGuard configs in the client area.
IVPN. Audited, no-logs posture, accepts anonymous payment.
Comparable to Mullvad; a reasonable alternative if you prefer their jurisdiction or pricing.
Not importable here: Riseup ships its own Bitmask client rather than WireGuard .conf files. Install their app instead — but note it will take the VPN slot from this scanner.
Riseup, a long-standing activist collective with a strong record.
Excellent trustworthiness for activists, but it is a separate app, so it cannot coexist with this scanner either.

Avoid free VPN apps from app stores.
Measured findings, not opinion: • Of the top 150 free VPN Android apps, 1 in 5 were flagged as potential malware and a quarter had privacy-breaking defects such as DNS leaks (CSIRO / ICSI / UC Berkeley / UNSW, 2017). • CNET\'s 2024 research found more than 60% of free VPN apps raised privacy concerns. • Repeated disclosures have found free VPN apps logging and selling user traffic, and shipping trackers and malware.
Free VPN apps are usually paid for with your data. For someone being targeted for surveillance, that trades one observer for another — and this time you consented.
If you cannot self-host and cannot pay, prefer the entries above, which publish real WireGuard configurations you can inspect as text and import here.
